short: Electron Backscatter Diffraction (EBSD) analysis of laser-cl
title: Electron Backscatter Diffraction (EBSD) analysis of laser-cladded AISI 420 martensitic stainless steel

lanes.label: Classical tools
lanes.sub: collapsed to one node per state

states.title: Hypothesis and design
states.head: Crystallographic (EBSD) basis of microstructure evolution and residual stress across zones of laser-cladded 420 martensitic stainless steel is not established. EBSD image quality (IQ), degraded by lattice distortion, should reveal the residual stress distribution across the clad zones.
states.detail: Absorbed: n1 (HYP/gap), n2 (HYP/hypothesis), n3 (DES/base_system), n4 (DES/method), n5 (PRC/deposition)

states.title: Structure state
states.head: Bead cross-section divides into bead zone, dilution zone, a curved interface and the heat-affected zone of the substrate. Prior-austenite grains change from planar at the interface to long columnar in DZ(I), mixed in DZ(C) and equiaxed in BZ.
states.detail: Absorbed: n6 (STR/microstructure/distribution), n9 (STR/microstructure/shape), n7 (STR/phase/identity), n11 (STR/microstructure/feature_size), n12 (STR/defect/extended), n13 (STR/phase/lattice). Premises: GOS of a grain is the mean misorientation between the grain-average orientation and all its pixels; EBSD IQ scales with Kikuchi-pattern sharpness and drops with dislocations, lattice strain and distortion

states.title: Property state and mechanisms
states.head: Solidification starts with planar grains at the fusion interface, grows epitaxial columnar austenite, and G/R changes shift it towards equiaxed grains up the bead. Extremely high, zone-dependent cooling during cladding transforms the austenite fully to martensite below Ms at different rates in each zone.
states.detail: Absorbed: n10 (MEC/pathway), n8 (MEC/pathway), n14 (PRP/value), n15 (MEC/pathway). Premises: Planar-then-epitaxial columnar solidification from the fusion line is usual in laser welding and cladding; Authors' earlier study found differential cooling rates and varying martensite and dislocation density across these clad zones; EBSD IQ scales with Kikuchi-pattern sharpness and drops with dislocations, lattice strain and distortion

states.title: Performance state
states.head: EBSD IQ mapping tracks the residual-stress distribution across bead, dilution and HAZ zones of the single-bead clad

states.title: Conclusion
states.head: EBSD resolves PAG morphology, martensite size, GOS and IQ gradients in laser-cladded 420 MSS; IQ is inversely related to residual stress and can evaluate its distribution

nodes.title: evidence, F2, F7
nodes.head: Pattern-quality maps: BZ(C) shows the finest lath contrast; DZ(C) and DZ(I) show coarser blocks and longer laths. Grain-size distribution: BZ tops out near 17.5 um and leads below ~5.5 um; DZ and DZ(I) extend to ~24 um
nodes.solves: Martensite substructure grains are coarser in both dilution-zone positions than in the bead zone
nodes.op: compare across conditions, measure feature metric
nodes.note: F2 image is paper Fig. 3 (PQ maps); difference is visible but qualitative at 60 um field width BZ peak ~10.5% at ~5.3 um, DZ peak ~11.4% at ~6.7 um; dashed divider at ~5.7 um (text says 6 um)

nodes.title: SEM, F10, F8, F9
nodes.head: GOS fractions: BZ has ~0.24 of grains at 3-5 deg vs ~0.17 in DZ; DZ has ~0.78 at 0-3 deg. GOS fractions: HAZ has ~0.43 of grains at 3-5 deg plus ~0.13 above 5 deg; DZ(I) ~0.65 at 0-3 deg; IZ in between.
nodes.solves: Bead-zone and HAZ grains carry more intragranular misorientation (plastic strain) than dilution-zone grains
nodes.op: compare across conditions, cross check consistency
nodes.note: bars: BZ 0.16/0.255/0.305/0.19/0.045/0.02, DZ 0.165/0.275/0.34/0.13/0.04/0.02; text 26% and 78% text: HAZ 59% high-GOS, DZ(I) 65% low-GOS; F9a SEM panel only locates zones paper acknowledges the contradiction and blames GOS parameters
nodes.detail: o8: GOS fractions: BZ has ~0.24 of grains at 3-5 deg vs ~0.17 in DZ; DZ has ~0.78 at 0-3 deg; o9: GOS fractions: HAZ has ~0.43 of grains at 3-5 deg plus ~0.13 above 5 deg; DZ(I) ~0.65 at 0-3 deg; IZ in between; a1: HAZ has the largest high-GOS fraction (F9c) yet higher IQ than DZ(I) in the same scan (F10f,g): GOS and IQ disagree on strain
nodes.necessity_reason: Only figure-backed support with image_support shown for n12 (o8, o9, a1).

nodes.title: evidence, F10
nodes.head: BZ(C) grain-average IQ rises with depth, fit line ~270 to ~390 over 0-300 um. DZ(C) IQ falls from ~345 at the top to ~275 near 200 um, then flattens.
nodes.solves: Lattice distortion varies with depth: falls down the bead zone, rises down DZ(C), falls from DZ(I) to the interface, rises into the HAZ
nodes.op: correlate across series, cross check consistency, read trend
nodes.note: map a: bluer at top, greener below; colour bar 142-1308 while text quotes range 142-485 text states both 'decreased from higher to lower' and 'towards the bottom IQ is increased'; the plot supports the decrease, with only a slight end rise; many zero-IQ points plotted panels f and g; zero-IQ points in g
nodes.detail: o10: BZ(C) grain-average IQ rises with depth, fit line ~270 to ~390 over 0-300 um; o11: DZ(C) IQ falls from ~345 at the top to ~275 near 200 um, then flattens; o12: IQ rises through DZ(I) towards the interface (~1130 to ~1630), then falls from ~2000 to ~1400 moving into the HAZ

nodes.title: XRD, F11
nodes.head: Centreline residual stress: ~+380-555 at top, falls through the bead zone to negative values, reaches -810 to -1005 near 1200 um, positive again below ~1450 um
nodes.solves: Residual stress is tensile at the bead top, turns compressive at the bead-zone end, peaks compressive in the dilution zone and returns tensile in the HAZ
nodes.op: correlate across series, cross check consistency, read trend
nodes.note: contour of experimental centreline XRD plus simulated +/-300 um data from earlier work

nodes.title: MECH:tensile, F10, F11
nodes.head: IQ-RS inversion is inconsistent: IQ rises as signed RS falls in BZ and falls as RS turns tensile in HAZ, but falls in DZ as RS turns more compressive. Scan IQ averages differ fourfold (BZ 311, DZ(C) 300 vs DZ(I) 1255, HAZ 1626) with different colour-bar ranges, so IQ is only comparable within a scan
nodes.solves: EBSD IQ mapping tracks the residual-stress distribution across bead, dilution and HAZ zones of the single-bead clad
nodes.note: inverse to signed RS in BZ/HAZ, inverse to |RS| in DZ; the paper's 'inversely proportional' mixes the two ranked across scans, IQ would call BZ more distorted than DZ(I), opposite to F11 where DZ carries the largest |RS|
nodes.detail: a2: IQ-RS inversion is inconsistent: IQ rises as signed RS falls in BZ and falls as RS turns tensile in HAZ, but falls in DZ as RS turns more compressive; a3: Scan IQ averages differ fourfold (BZ 311, DZ(C) 300 vs DZ(I) 1255, HAZ 1626) with different colour-bar ranges, so IQ is only comparable within a scan
nodes.inner_audit: a3: ranked across scans, IQ would call BZ more distorted than DZ(I), opposite to F11 where DZ carries the largest |RS|
